proof_summary: A Fibonacci-type sequence of exponents is shown inductively to tend to infinity and to satisfy $2^{f(n)}\mid a_n,b_n$, since each recurrence term is a product of the two preceding pairs. A finite 12-cycle computation modulo $15$ shows $a_n\ne0$; hence, for each fixed $k>1$, eventually $a_n$ has at least $k$ factors equal to $2$, so its $k$-th prime factor is constantly $2$ (period $1$).
